fields.features_heading: What the Agent Knows Before the First Showing
fields.features_subheading: A buyer answers once, on a phone. The agent starts the first call already knowing the budget and the deadline.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the buyer's situation

Ask whether the buyer owns a home now. A yes opens questions on whether it has to sell first and when it lists. A renter is asked when the lease ends instead, so nobody reads both.
fields.feature_2:
The preapproval letter, read into fields

Let buyers upload a preapproval letter. The form reads the lender and the loan amount into the buyer's record, and any value it cannot read goes to the agent to confirm by hand.
fields.feature_3:
Must-haves kept apart from wish lists

Ask for bedrooms and the longest commute the buyer will accept as must-haves, then for a separate list of nice-to-haves. Search on the first list and use the second to break ties.
fields.feature_4:
Every buyer lands with one agent

Assign each buyer to the agent who covers the neighborhoods they picked, with the full answers in an email or a Slack message. Buyers on a tight move date reach that agent first.
fields.feature_5:
The buyer agreement on the last screen

Place your written buyer agreement after the final question and collect a typed or drawn signature. The signed copy is saved to the buyer's record with the date it was signed.
fields.feature_6:
Code your brokerage can keep

Export the full code of the form and its buyer database to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can then connect it to the CRM or transaction software your office runs.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Kinds of Buyer, Four Next Steps
fields.tab_content_1:
When a buyer has no preapproval, a consult comes first

Dara Whitfield is buying her first home through Ansel Park Realty. She sets a budget of $425,000 and answers "Not yet" when the form asks about a preapproval letter. Any buyer without one is offered a 30-minute buyer consultation, and the showing request opens after it. Dara books the first open slot.
fields.tab_content_2:
Relocating in 45 days or less puts the agent on alert

Nadia Ferrer starts a new job in Columbus and has to move in 32 days. She tells Sorrel Bay Realty she can only tour by live video for now. Any move date within 45 days sends her agent, Calvin Shore, a Slack message with her answers. He lines up three video tours before the weekend.
fields.tab_content_3:
Any buyer with $800,000 or more goes to the luxury lead

Rookmere Realty splits the county between two area agents, and each buyer lands with the agent who covers them. A budget of $800,000 or more overrides the area and goes to Mei Lindqvist, the luxury lead. Of the four buyers who applied this morning, only Anouk Bell, at $950,000, is hers.
fields.tab_content_4:
All showings wait on a signed buyer agreement

The last screen at Willow Gate Realty is its written buyer agreement. An MLS participant working with a buyer has to sign one with that buyer before the first tour, so the form keeps the showing request locked until the signature is in. Marcus Quill reads the 90-day term and signs, then asks to see 14 Quince Lane.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Real Estate Buyer Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build a real estate buyer intake form that sorts each new buyer before the first showing.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List what you ask at the first meeting
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask about the home, not the buyer
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every question you ask a new buyer at the first meeting, such as budget and target areas. Mark the answers that change what you do next, such as a missing preapproval letter or a lease that ends soon.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask about bedrooms and commute limits, and leave the buyer's personal traits off the form. The Fair Housing Act prohibits discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, disability, and familial status.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pair each answer that matters with what should happen next. A buyer without preapproval can book a consultation. A move inside your cutoff can message the agent. Budgets past a set amount can skip the area agents and go to a specialist.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Close the form with the written buyer agreement your brokerage uses, with the term and search area filled in from the answers. Have your broker or counsel approve the wording, and the fields it fills, before the form goes live.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your questions and rules into one plain-English prompt. Emergent builds the form with its routing rules and the buyer database behind it. To add an agent later, describe the change in a new prompt. The live form updates.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Connect the tools your office uses
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send alerts to the inbox or Slack channel each agent watches. If your office runs a CRM with an API, connect it so every new buyer arrives there as a contact, with the intake answers attached to the record.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it as three different buyers
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit the form as a first-time buyer without a preapproval letter, then as a relocating buyer, then as a high-budget buyer. Check that each one triggers the right step and reaches the right agent. Then share the live link with new buyers.

faq_plan.q: What is a real estate buyer intake form?
faq_plan.a: A real estate buyer intake form is the questionnaire an agent sends a new homebuyer before the first meeting. It records what the buyer can spend and when they need to move, plus where they want to live. The agent plans the search and the next step for that buyer from those answers.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a real estate buyer intake form?
faq_plan.a: List the questions you ask at a first buyer meeting and what each answer should trigger, then describe both in a prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. Emergent builds the form and the database it saves each buyer to. Submit a few test buyers and prompt any change until each one lands where it should.

faq_plan.q: What questions go on a real estate buyer intake form?
faq_plan.a: Ask for contact details, budget, preapproval status, move date, target neighborhoods, and whether a current home has to sell first. Ask for must-haves such as bedrooms and parking apart from nice-to-haves. Close with how the buyer prefers to tour and to be contacted.

faq_plan.q: Should a real estate buyer intake form ask about preapproval?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask whether the buyer has a preapproval letter, because the answer decides what you do first. The CFPB describes it as a statement from a lender that they are tentatively willing to lend money to you, up to a certain loan amount. Leave lender choice and loan terms to the buyer and their lender.

faq_plan.q: What should a real estate buyer intake form leave out?
faq_plan.a: Leave out questions about the buyer's race, religion, national origin, sex, disability, or whether children will live in the home. Federal fair housing law covers each of those traits. Ask about the property instead, such as bedrooms or accessibility features the buyer wants the home to have.

faq_plan.q: Can a real estate buyer intake form include the buyer agreement?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The form can show your written buyer agreement on its last screen and capture a typed or drawn signature, saved to the buyer's record. Have your broker approve the wording first, including how it discloses the amount or rate of any compensation.

faq_plan.q: When should an agent send a real estate buyer intake form?
faq_plan.a: Send it as soon as a buyer reaches out, before the first call or consultation. The answers let you prepare for that call with the budget and target areas in hand. Send it again to past buyers who come back, since their situation may have changed.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a real estate buyer intake form have?
faq_plan.a: Keep it to what you need before the first conversation, about 15 to 20 questions, and let branching hide the rest. A renter never sees questions about selling a current home. Emergent puts no cap on responses.

faq_plan.q: How can a real estate buyer intake form assign buyers to agents?
faq_plan.a: Set a rule for each answer that matters: neighborhoods map to the agent who covers them, and budgets above a set amount go to a specialist. The form applies the rule on submit and alerts that agent by email or Slack. Every buyer also stays in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What happens after a buyer submits a real estate buyer intake form?
faq_plan.a: The buyer should see a confirmation with the next step, and the assigned agent should get the answers. Set the next step by answer, such as a consultation for buyers without preapproval or a call for buyers moving soon. Apps built on Emergent sync with any CRM that has an API, which saves retyping each buyer by hand.
